This scheme of work is designed using the **TALULAR** framework (**T**eaching **a**nd **L**earning **u**sing **L**ocally **a**vailable **R**esources), which is highly effective in Malawian rural schools. With 55 students and 14 textbooks (1 per 4 students), the class will be organized into **11 stable learning groups of 5 students** (with one group of 6). Each group will share one textbook, sit together, and work collaboratively. --- ### **6-Week Scheme of Work Outline: Basic Statistics (Grade 8)** | Week | Topic | Key Concepts | TALULAR / Practical Resources | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1** | **Introduction to Data & Collection** | Definition of data; Qualitative vs. Quantitative; Tally charts. | Schoolyard plants/crops, student birth months, chalkboard. | | **2** | **Organizing Data** | Frequency tables; Grouped vs. Ungrouped data. | Stones, bottle tops (*zivindiki*), student exercise books. | | **3** | **Data Representation I** | Pictograms and Bar Charts (drawing scales without graph paper). | Charcoal/chalk on ground or chalkboard, sticks, rulers. | | **4** | **Data Representation II** | Introduction to Pie Charts (using simple fractions: $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{1}{8}$). | Plastic plates/cups to draw circles, mud/clay models. | | **5** | **Measures of Central Tendency** | Mean, Median, and Mode (conceptual and computational). | Maize seeds, stones, student heights (standing in line). | | **6** | **Interpretation & Review** | Reading graphs; Misleading statistics; End of unit assessment. | Chalkboard-drawn scenarios, group presentations. | --- ### **Detailed Activities for Week 1: Introduction to Data and Data Collection** #### **Week 1 Objectives:** By the end of this week, students will be able to: 1. Define "data" in their own words. 2. Distinguish between qualitative (descriptive) and quantitative (numerical) data. 3. Collect and record data using a tally system. 4. Work cooperatively in their assigned textbook groups. --- #### **Lesson 1: What is Data? (40 Minutes)** * **Objective:** Define data and identify qualitative vs. quantitative data. * **Resources:** Chalkboard, student notebooks, 1 textbook per group. | Time | Activity | Teacher Action | Student Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **10 min** | **Introduction & Grouping** | Assign students into their 11 permanent groups of 5. Distribute the 14 textbooks (1 per group). Write the word **"DATA"** on the board. Ask: *"What do you think this means?"* | Sit in assigned groups. Discuss the word "Data" with group members. | | **15 min** | **Concept Delivery** | Explain that data is "information collected for learning or decision-making." Write definitions on the board:
1. **Qualitative** (descriptive, e.g., favorite crop: maize, cassava, groundnuts).
2. **Quantitative** (numerical, e.g., number of siblings). | Copy definitions into notebooks. Read the introductory page of the textbook chapter aloud within their groups (one student reads, others listen). | | **10 min** | **Guided Practice** | Write 5 examples on the board (e.g., color of eyes, height of maize plants, number of desks, names of villages). Ask groups to classify them. | In groups, discuss and classify the 5 examples as Qualitative or Quantitative. | | **5 min** | **Wrap-up** | Call on different groups to share their answers. Summarize the lesson. | Write down the correct classifications in notebooks. | --- #### **Lesson 2: Methods of Data Collection (40 Minutes)** * **Objective:** Understand how data is gathered (observation, counting, surveys). * **Resources:** Chalkboard, local environment. | Time | Activity | Teacher Action | Student Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **5 min** | **Recall** | Ask: *"What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative data?"* | Respond verbally. | | **15 min** | **Instruction** | Explain three ways to collect data:
1. **Observation** (watching and recording).
2. **Counting** (measuring physical items).
3. **Survey** (asking questions).
Draw a simple 3-column table on the board showing these methods. | Copy the table into notebooks. Discuss in groups which method they would use to find out the favorite football team of the class. | | **15 min** | **Practical Fieldwork (No Tech)** | Lead the class outside to the schoolyard. Assign each group a specific task:
- *Groups 1-4:* Count the number of trees in a specific area (Counting).
- *Groups 5-8:* Observe and record the colors of clothing worn by classmates (Observation).
- *Groups 9-11:* Ask 10 students from another class their favorite subject (Survey). | Go outside in groups. Work together to collect the assigned data on a scrap piece of paper. | | **5 min** | **Debrief** | Lead the class back inside. Ask groups to briefly state what data they collected. | Return to desks and prepare to use this data in the next lesson. | --- #### **Lesson 3: The Tally System (40 Minutes)** * **Objective:** Use tally marks to record data efficiently. * **Resources:** Chalkboard, chalk. | Time | Activity | Teacher Action | Student Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **10 min** | **Demonstration** | Explain that counting large numbers can be confusing. Introduce **Tally Marks** ($I, II, III, IIII, \cancel{IIII}$). Show how the diagonal line represents "5" and makes counting in blocks of 5 easy. | Practice drawing tallies in notebooks as the teacher demonstrates on the board. | | **15 min** | **Board Practice** | Write a random list of letters on the board representing favorite local foods: `M, C, M, G, M, C, C, M, G, M, M, C` (M = Maize, C = Cassava, G = Groundnuts). Show how to cross out each letter and make a tally. | Watch the demonstration, then copy the list and complete the tally chart in notebooks. | | **10 min** | **Group Work** | Ask groups to open their textbook to the exercise on "Tallying" (typically a list of numbers or items). | Share the textbook. Work together to convert the textbook data list into a tally chart in their notebooks. | | **5 min** | **Peer Check** | Write the correct tally chart on the board. | Compare group work with the board and self-correct. | --- #### **Lesson 4: Practical Project - Class Survey (40 Minutes)** * **Objective:** Conduct a full data collection cycle using tallies. * **Resources:** Chalkboard, student notebooks. | Time | Activity | Teacher Action | Student Action | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **5 min** | **Set-up** | Write the project topic on the board: **"Birth Months of Grade 8 Students."** Draw a blank table with two columns: *Month* (January to December) and *Tally*. | Copy the blank table into notebooks. | | **20 min** | **Data Collection (Active)** | Call out the months one by one: *"Who was born in January? Stand up."* Count the standing students. | If born in the called month, stand up. All students record the tally marks in their notebooks for each month based on how many students stand up. | | **10 min** | **Group Analysis** | Ask groups to look at their completed tally table and answer three questions written on the board:
1. *Which month has the most births?*
2. *Which month has the fewest births?*
3. *What is the total number of students surveyed?* | Work in groups of 5 to analyze their tally charts and write down the answers to the questions. | | **5 min** | **Conclusion** | Ask different groups to share their answers. Explain that next week, they will turn these tallies into "frequencies" (numbers). | Pack up books. Ensure the textbook is returned to the group leader/teacher. | --- ### **Teacher Tips for this Context:** 1. **Chalkboard Management:** Since there are no printouts, write the lesson outline and key tables on the board *before* class starts (during break time) to maximize teaching time. 2. **Textbook Care:** Assign one "Textbook Monitor" per group who is responsible for collecting and keeping the book safe. 3. **Inclusivity:** Ensure that girls and boys are mixed equally in the 11 groups, and encourage quieter students to be the ones who write or speak for the group.
